entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theotgaud was the archbishop of Trier from 850 until his deposition in 867. He was the abbot of Mettlach prior to his election in 847 to succeed his uncle, Hetto, as archbishop.

 Theotgaud played a significant role in the Frankish Empire during the Carolingian Renaissance, a period marked by a resurgence of classical learning and culture. He was a key figure in the development of the liturgical practices and hymnology of the Carolingian era.

 Theotgaud's legacy can be seen in the numerous manuscripts and illuminated texts that he commissioned during his tenure as archbishop. These works, such as the 'Glossa Ordinaria' and the 'Liber Hymnorum', showcase the enduring influence of the Carolingian era on Western liturgical practices.

 As the founder of the monastery of Mettlach, Theotgaud helped establish a center of learning and spirituality that would serve as a model for future monastic institutions in Europe.

 'The Lord's Prayer is the most beautiful of all prayers, for it is the very word of God.' - Theotgaud
